about: The Introit of the First Sunday of Advent, the Mass that opens the liturgical year. Its antiphon is Psalm 24:1-3 in the Vulgate numbering (Psalm 25 in Hebrew) and its verse is the fourth verse of the same psalm. The Offertory of this Mass returns to the same three verses.

s01.translation: To You, O my God, I lift up my soul. In You I trust. Let me not be put to shame, nor let my enemies mock me, for none who await You shall be put to shame.

s02.translation: Make Your ways known to me, O Lord, and teach me Your paths.

s03.translation: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

s04.narrative: After the doxology the priest repeats the Introit antiphon from Ad te levávi to the psalm verse.

s05.translation: To You, O my God, I lift up my soul. In You I trust. Let me not be put to shame, nor let my enemies mock me, for none who await You shall be put to shame.

w012.function: Present subjunctive in a petition: the psalmist asks not to be put to shame. The Hebrew volitive form and Greek optative confirm this reading.
w012.note: The ending -am is future indicative and present subjunctive at once. This edition takes the subjunctive and marks the doubt.

w017.function: A masculine nominative plural agreeing with “inimíci” (w016).

w019.function: The adjective stands substantivally for all people. Its relative clause identifies them as those who await the Lord.

w035.function: The doxology has no expressed verb. It supplies the wish “glory be” from liturgical usage.
